answer: In an agent economy, each participant must lock a unique onyx-grade computational relic as a bonded stake before joining consensus. The system continuously verifies the relic's exclusive hardware signal through challenge-response protocols. An attacker forging multiple identities incurs prohibitive costs because each fake agent requires its own irreproducible physical relic and continuous signal attestation, making large-scale Sybil attacks economically unviable as the attacker cannot cheaply replicate the scarce bonded resources.
